questions.q: Express $2\sin(5x)\cos(3x)$ as a sum of trigonometric functions.
questions.answer: Using the product-to-sum identity $2\sin A \cos B = \sin(A + B) + \sin(A - B)$ gives $\sin(8x) + \sin(2x)$.
Using sum-to-product: numerator $= 2\sin(2x)\cos(x)$ and denominator $= 2\cos(2x)\cos(x)$. Dividing gives $\frac{\sin(2x)}{\cos(2x)} = \tan(2x)$.

questions.q: What is the exact value of $\cos(105^\circ) - \cos(15^\circ)$?
What geometric curve is represented by the polar equation $r = 2 + 2\cos\theta$?
questions.answer: An equation of the form $r = a + a\cos\theta$ has equal coefficients ($a = b$), which represents a cardioid (heart-shaped curve).

questions.q: How many petals does the rose curve $r = 4\cos(3\theta)$ have?
questions.answer: For a rose curve $r = a\cos(n\theta)$, if $n$ is odd, the curve has $n$ petals. Here $n = 3$, so it has $3$ petals.

questions.q: How many petals does the rose curve $r = 2\sin(4\theta)$ have?
questions.answer: If $n$ is even in $r = a\sin(n\theta)$, the curve has $2n$ petals. Here $n = 4$, so it has $2(4) = 8$ petals.

questions.q: Convert the polar point $(4, \frac{5\pi}{6})$ to rectangular coordinates $(x, y)$.
Convert the rectangular point $(-3, -3)$ to polar coordinates with $r > 0$ and $0 \leq \theta < 2\pi$.
What is the Cartesian equation for the polar line $\theta = \frac{\pi}{3}$?
questions.answer: Take tangent of both sides: $\tan\theta = \tan(\frac{\pi}{3}) = \sqrt{3}$. Since $\tan\theta = \frac{y}{x}$, we have $\frac{y}{x} = \sqrt{3} \Rightarrow y = \sqrt{3}x$.

questions.q: Find all solutions to $\sin(2x) = \cos(x)$ in the interval $[0, 2\pi)$.
questions.answer: $2\sin x \cos x - \cos x = 0 \Rightarrow \cos x(2\sin x - 1) = 0$. $\cos x = 0 \Rightarrow x = \frac{\pi}{2}, \frac{3\pi}{2}$. $\sin x = \frac{1}{2} \Rightarrow x = \frac{\pi}{6}, \frac{5\pi}{6}$.
Since $-1 \leq \sin(4x) \leq 1$, we have $-3 \leq -3\sin(4x) \leq 3$. Adding $2$ gives $-1 \leq f(x) \leq 5$.
